recommendation: A1: choose option (a) only; D-273 stands and D-272 remains CONTESTED history, with no D-000 amendment. A2: choose option (ii); record one direct user disposition confirming that the nine parked CONTESTED headings remain historical, their adopted resolvers stand, and none is reopened. Leave every existing heading unchanged.
rationale: D-000 clause 2 already makes termination mandatory after three exchanges per party, and D-272 records that the fourth exchange was outside that rule and that turn 3 was the terminal merits review. D-273 and both of its reviews preserve that disposition, so a new rule purporting to create a D-093 exception would add ambiguity: D-093 expressly says its freeze-precondition redispatch was turn 3, not a fourth turn. A2 is different. The bytes show nine parked headings covering the listed decisions, an adopted resolver for every subject, and no live authority dependency on a parked entry. A direct user entry is useful there because it records the result of the batch sent to the user and satisfies D-000 clause 3 without rewriting history or reopening a successor.

refutations.claim: D-272 already records that D-000 clause 2 forbids the fourth exchange and that turn 3 is the terminal merits review.
refutations.evidence: COORD D-272 Status says the fourth exchange was Dual OBJECT, was not D-000 consensus, and was not the terminal merits review; it identifies turn 3 Dual OBJECT as terminal.

refutations.claim: Both D-273 reviewers rechecked and accepted D-272's custody of the rejected fourth exchange.
refutations.evidence: The Claude D-273 review refutes the attack that the history was understated by quoting D-272's disposition; the Codex D-273 review says the hash-pinned D-272 entry preserves the prior subjects, verdicts, positions, and fourth-exchange rejection.

refutations.claim: Nothing live depends on D-272 being adopted.
refutations.evidence: File 08 contains no D-272 reference. Later COORD references describe it as CONTESTED or explicitly exclude it from the adoption branch, and D-273 records the same frozen artifact in a new cycle.

refutations.claim: D-000 has an interpretive gap that should be closed by expressly forbidding a fourth exchange.
refutations.evidence: D-000 clause 2 is titled 'Termination clause: 3 turns each side' and commands that, absent consensus after three exchanges per party, the decision is recorded CONTESTED, parked, and batched to the user. D-272 applies that text without identifying ambiguity.

refutations.claim: D-093 supplies a fourth-exchange exception that should be generalized in D-000.
refutations.evidence: COORD D-093 says the turn-3 review was re-dispatched after a freeze-digest mismatch and expressly says this was 'not a fourth turn' because the first turn-3 verdicts were freeze-precondition OBJECTs rather than merits reviews.

refutations.claim: A protocol amendment has the same cost as a bare historical note.
refutations.evidence: Both can occupy one direct-user heading, but their legal effects differ: D-054 is a substantive user amendment, while a note does not change D-000. Adding a generalized redispatch rule changes future cycle authority and therefore carries scope and wording risk absent from a historical confirmation.

refutations.claim: A2 comprises nine CONTESTED headings whose subjects all have adopted resolvers.
refutations.evidence: The nine headings are D-017/D-019-D-024, D-051/D-052/D-053, D-059, D-067, D-094, D-095, D-098, D-099, and D-101. Their subjects are resolved by D-028 through D-030, D-036, D-037, D-047, D-048, D-064, D-069 through D-072, D-096, and D-102 as mapped in the packet and confirmed in COORD.

refutations.claim: The parked A2 entries have no live authority dependents.
refutations.evidence: File 08 has no strict-boundary hit for the listed decision identifiers. Surviving COORD and artifact references are historical, retarget authority to adopted successors, or state that a successor is a new cycle and does not overturn the CONTESTED history.

refutations.claim: Option (i) would leave the user's disposition of the clause-2 batch unrecorded in COORD.
refutations.evidence: Under option (i), only the existing CONTESTED entries and the external owner reply would exist; no register entry would state that the owner reviewed the batch and declined to reopen it.

refutations.claim: Reopening any A2 subject would collide with an adopted successor chain.
refutations.evidence: COORD contains the adopted subject resolvers listed above, including later owner recordings and file-08 edits for several chains. Reopening would require the corresponding successor's own supersession or overturn procedure rather than merely changing a CONTESTED heading.

amendments: Remove A1 option (c1). Treat D-093 as a same-turn freeze-precondition redispatch precedent, not as a fourth-turn exception.
Use the direct user entry only for the A2 no-reopen disposition; do not relabel or rewrite any CONTESTED heading.
